title.en: Unit 10 · Power Series, Taylor & Maclaurin Series

chapterTag.category: AP Calc BC BC-6 — Power, Taylor & Maclaurin

body.en: Unit 10 · Power Series, Taylor & Maclaurin Series covers essential College Board AP Calculus BC competencies across foundational mechanics, intermediate analysis, and advanced FRQ problem solving.

blocks.heading: Level 1 · Foundations — Common Maclaurin Series & Taylor Formula

body.en: Taylor polynomials centered at x = c and standard Maclaurin series for e^x, sin x, cos x, and 1/(1-x).

\[ e^x = \sum_{n=0}^\infty \frac{x^n}{n!}, \quad \sin x = \sum_{n=0}^\infty \frac{(-1)^n x^{2n+1}}{(2n+1)!}, \quad \cos x = \sum_{n=0}^\infty \frac{(-1)^n x^{2n}}{(2n)!}, \quad \frac{1}{1-x} = \sum_{n=0}^\infty x^n. \]

question.en:
Level 1 · Foundations

Write the first four non-zero terms of the Maclaurin series for \(f(x) = \cos(2x)\).

blocks.heading: Level 2 · Medium — Radius and Interval of Convergence for Power Series

body.en: Use the Ratio Test to find the radius of convergence R, and test endpoints separately to determine the interval of convergence.

caption.en: sin(x) vs. the current Maclaurin polynomial T(x)

question.en:
Level 2 · Medium

Find the radius and interval of convergence of the power series \(\sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{(x - 2)^n}{n \cdot 3^n}\).

solution.en:
Apply the Ratio Test: \[ \lim_{n\to\infty} \left| \frac{(x-2)^{n+1}}{(n+1)3^{n+1}} \cdot \frac{n3^n}{(x-2)^n} \right| = \frac{|x-2|}{3} < 1 \implies |x - 2| < 3 \implies R = 3. \] Interval interior: \(-1 < x < 5\).
At \(x = 5\): \(\sum \frac{3^n}{n3^n} = \sum \frac{1}{n}\) (divergent harmonic series).
At \(x = -1\): \(\sum \frac{(-3)^n}{n3^n} = \sum \frac{(-1)^n}{n}\) (convergent alternating harmonic series).
Interval of convergence: \([-1, 5)\).

blocks.heading: Level 3 · Advanced — Taylor Series Error Bounds (Lagrange & Alternating)

body.en: Alternating Series Error Bound and Lagrange Error Bound for remainder estimation.

question.en:
Level 3 · Advanced

The function \(f(x)\) has derivatives satisfying \(|f^{(4)}(x)| \le 12\) for all \(x \in [0, 0.5]\). If \(f(0.5)\) is approximated by its 3rd-degree Taylor polynomial centered at 0, find a bound on the maximum error using the Lagrange Error Bound.
